solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A new parent, shattered, arranged to return before dinner

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so these letters are scrambled
to return is to come back, so the synonym for arranged is read backwards

parts.note: laid, as in a table laid or arranged for a meal

explanation.surface: Someone sets out, in a muddle, a new and exhausted parent's things before the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' scrambles PARENT into TEPRAN, and 'to return' turns LAID into DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-based adjective is a formal synonym for what happens prior to a meal, prandium being Latin for lunch.

clue.text: Note if Rolls gets makeover that's basic

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce restyled becomes a plain, stripped-down car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets makeover' scrambles N, IF and ROLLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something plain with no extras or luxuries, simple and basic.

clue.text: Imitate nymph

definitions.meaning: to repeat or copy what someone else says or does
the mountain nymph of Greek myth who pined away until only her voice remained

explanation.definitionFit: Copying another's words is one sense; the other is the name of the mythical nymph whose voice lingered.

clue.text: Hired mob going wild tear down 19 around end of November

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the other pieces
going wild means getting out of control, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: 19 points to the answer at 19-down, a word whose standard abbreviation is C

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A paid gang runs riot, pulling down a building around the end of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wild' gives RENTAOWD, which 'around' puts round CR. The 19 is the answer at 19-down, abbreviated C as on Oxbridge college lists.
explanation.definitionFit: A term for people paid to attend and swell an audience or protest, so a mob that is hired.

clue.text: Refuse vote against state

parts.note: nay is a vote against, as opposed to aye
to say is to state

explanation.surface: Turning down a vote against a state.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny or say no to something, especially habitually, is to refuse it.

clue.text: Haematite obtained from robust seaweed

parts.note: iron as an adjective means strong and robust, as in an iron constitution
ore, or oarweed, is a dialect name for a kind of seaweed

explanation.surface: A mineral extracted from hardy marine plants.
explanation.walkthrough: ORE as seaweed is a crossword favourite from the word oarweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Haematite is a red mineral that is a chief source of the metal, an example of the type.

clue.text: City supporter aimlessly scribbles crosses

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a bra is a supporting undergarment
to doodle is to scribble without purpose

explanation.surface: A football fan idly scrawls marks on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: These dogs are crossbreeds of a Labrador and a poodle, so crosses in the breeding sense.

clue.text: Spot politician entering tall building

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP seen walking into a tower block.
explanation.definitionFit: A small blemish on the skin is a spot, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lie back following blow

indicators.note: back here means the word for lie is turned to run the other way

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone lies down again after being struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial synonym: a sharp punch or thump.

clue.text: Make smooth start to your search in maze

parts.note: to hone a blade is to make it smooth and sharp

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up the beginning of a hunt through a labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: A network of wax cells, or anything with that pattern, is a labyrinthine structure, so it can stand for a maze.

clue.text: George IV, perhaps, runs in furiously preening, etc

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other
furiously means wildly, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A vain royal dandy primps frantically before his mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' scrambles PREENING and ETC, and 'in' puts R among them.
explanation.definitionFit: George ruled as regent for his father before becoming king, an example of the title, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Enlist operator to be at centre of check

indicators.note: a piece placed at the centre of a word sits inside it

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: Signing up a machine operator to run a checkpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to persuade someone to join or take part, so to recruit.

clue.text: Lover boy's house in Florence next to river running west

parts.note: casa is Italian for house, and Florence is in Italy

indicators.note: in an across clue, running west means reading from right to left

parts.note: the Avon is a familiar English river

explanation.surface: A romantic young man has an Italian home beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian adventurer's name became a byword for a seducer or womaniser.

clue.text: With penetrating warble, Greek character so sounds like Ellington

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so the abbreviation goes into the word for warble

parts.note: to warble is to sing
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A Greek with a fluting voice sounds like Duke Ellington.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke Ellington was an American jazz bandleader of the big-band era.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellington's big band played the genre that dominated the 1930s, so his sound is an example of it.

clue.text: Irritating job for a seamstress?

parts.note: to needle is to irritate, and a job is work, so an irritating job read this way is the sewing a seamstress does

explanation.surface: A dressmaker has an annoying task to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing and embroidery done by hand with a threaded pin is exactly a seamstress's craft.

clue.text: Forbid to go back inside remote valley

indicators.note: going back means these letters are read in the reverse direction
the letters sit inside the words remote valley, spanning both

explanation.surface: Someone is banned from returning to an isolated valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' finds OTEV in 'remOTE Valley', and 'to go back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right of refusal over something is to prohibit it.

clue.text: Like rock when surrounded by sea

indicators.note: one piece surrounded by another sits inside it

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something behaves like a rock while ringed by ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Made of the dark volcanic stone basalt, so resembling or consisting of that rock.

clue.text: Cut top off fodder plant

indicators.note: taking the top off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: vetch is a leguminous plant grown as fodder for livestock

explanation.surface: Instructions to trim the tip of a crop grown for animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' drops the V of VETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave a design is to cut it into a surface with acid or a tool.

clue.text: Pass on third part of thesis to Trinity say

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
on is the leg side in cricket, so it gives leg

indicators.note: the third part of a word here is its third letter

explanation.surface: Handing in a section of a dissertation at Trinity.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity is an example of a Cambridge or Oxford institution of this kind, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Tired about absence of throne, like some in high places?

indicators.note: about here means one piece goes round another

parts.note: sapped means drained of energy, tired
NO signals absence, as in no entry
throne is slang for a toilet, abbreviated WC for water closet

explanation.surface: A worn-out monarch without a seat of power, like grandees in high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' is jokey slang for a lavatory, and 'absence of' is read as the word no; 'about' puts the pair inside.
explanation.definitionFit: High mountain peaks are white on top, so the question mark points to summits rather than powerful people.

clue.text: Being quietly different creates a fuss

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
other means different

explanation.surface: Being quiet and unconventional causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for commotion or bother, a synonym of to-do.

clue.text: We contributed to vote for old Tory MP

indicators.note: the pronoun contributes to the vote by going inside it

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Voters helped elect a former Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Enoch Powell was a controversial Conservative MP of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch Powell was a Conservative member of Parliament, an example of an old Tory MP.

clue.text: Nematodes or maggot-eating fish

indicators.note: a piece eating another takes it inside

parts.note: eels are fish
a maggot is a grub, loosely a worm

explanation.surface: Fish that feed on grubs, offered as an alternative to roundworms.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small parasitic roundworms, a type within the phylum Nematoda.

clue.text: Disguise bloke let out

parts.note: bloke is British slang for a man

indicators.note: out here means rearranged, put out of order

explanation.surface: A man in disguise has been released.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloak or covering that conceals, hence a figurative cover or disguise.

clue.text: Bones discovered after force leaves pit

indicators.note: when something leaves a word, it is removed

parts.note: a fossa is an anatomical pit or hollow
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Skeletal remains are unearthed after a team pulls out of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural of os, used in anatomy for skeletal bones.

clue.text: Have time for coffee before midday

definitions.text: Have time for coffee before midday

parts.words: Have time for coffee before midday
parts.note: the British mid-morning snack break is named after the hour, eleven o'clock, before noon

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a coffee break during the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the late-morning tea or coffee break is named after eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for a light snack and drink taken around eleven in the morning.

clue.text: Brief comment on website is quaint

indicators.note: brief here means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a tweet is a short comment posted on the Twitter website

explanation.surface: A short online remark is called charmingly old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' cuts the last T from TWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A British adjective for something affectedly dainty or sweet, close to quaint.

clue.text: Pools perturbed celebrant touring English church

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the other pieces
perturbed means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troubled priest travels round an English church, gambling on the pools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perturbed' gives TREBLANCE, which 'touring' splits round the abbreviations. The football pools is a British betting game on match results.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known bet on the British football pools, predicting score draws, stands for the pools.
